sources.name: UCI_SMS_Spam
sources.note: UCI SMS Spam Collection (University of California, Irvine). Labels: ham = legitimate, spam = scam.

sources.name: NCSU_SMS_Phishing
sources.note: NC State SMS phishing collection. The file has no label column; every row is a reported phishing message. Capped so scam messages do not swamp the legitimate ones.

sources.name: government_impersonation_synthetic
sources.note: Balanced, project-written synthetic government-impersonation examples and legitimate controls. Use for targeted coverage, not as evidence of real-world accuracy.

sources.name: reward_bonus_synthetic
sources.note: Balanced, project-written unsolicited high-bonus/reward promotion examples and legitimate controls. Synthetic spam labels broaden targeted training coverage; they are not evidence that a real offer is fraudulent.

sources.name: noticare_philippines
sources.note: 100 project-written Tagalog/Taglish seeds (unverified). Off by default: they were used to tune the rules, so keep them for testing unless you replace them with real, reviewed messages.

sources.name: reported_messages
sources.note: Admin dashboard export of Reported phishing messages. Review and anonymize every row before enabling.
